app.title: AMP Discovery — Antimicrobial Peptide Intelligence
app.summary: A person pastes a peptide sequence in single-letter code, or picks one from a list of built-in examples, and runs it through a trained classifier. The result panel shows the predicted class, its probability against a fixed decision threshold, a confidence band, the sequence coloured by residue type, and a radar of its physicochemical profile. Tabbed views then break the call down: per-feature contributions ranked by magnitude and split into those pushing each way, the same sequence scored by three models with a vote and an average, and the full feature table, which can be downloaded as CSV. Two further tabs turn the profile into bench guidance keyed to thresholds, and let the person move property sliders to see how a simplified score would shift.

task.text: Score one peptide sequence for a predicted class, read which sequence properties drove the score, and decide whether the candidate is worth taking to the bench.

data.text: One peptide sequence in single-letter amino acid code, from which a fixed set of physicochemical and composition features is computed, plus per-feature attribution values and one probability per model.
data.item: a single peptide sequence of 10 to 100 residues

stage.text: screening candidate sequences before any bench work, to choose which ones to test

mechanism.text: A paste box with an example picker feeds a single-item analysis page, where a result card, a coloured sequence strip and a radar of normalised properties sit side by side, and five tabs below hold the attribution bars, the three-model comparison, the feature table with its export, the threshold-keyed guidance, and a slider panel that recomputes a simplified score live. A left sidebar switches between the analysis page and three static pages describing the training data and model scores.

field.text: sequence-based peptide activity prediction with feature attribution, in computational biology

workflow.name: score one item with a trained model and read why, then decide whether to pursue it

steps.here: a peptide sequence is pasted into a monospace box, or loaded from a named example list; it is upper-cased, stripped of whitespace, and rejected unless it is 10–100 standard residues

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: physicochemical and composition features are computed, scaled, and run through the gradient-boosted model to give a probability, classed against a fixed threshold of 0.40 chosen to limit missed positives

the sequence is redrawn with each residue coloured by charge or hydrophobicity class, with property chips for length, charge, hydrophobicity and isoelectric point, and a radar of five properties normalised to field-typical ranges

steps.step: see which inputs drove the computed value
steps.here: feature contributions are sorted by absolute size, drawn as a diverging bar chart of the top twelve, and listed as two ranked sets of up to six bars each, one pushing toward each class
three models score the same sequence; a bar chart against a 0.5 line, a vote count out of three and an average probability resolve to one of three verdicts, with disagreement flagged as borderline
every computed feature is tabled with its value and category, and downloaded as a CSV named after the first residues of the sequence

steps.step: plan the follow-up work from the computed profile
steps.here: the assay planner emits handling, solubility and stability notes keyed to charge, hydrophobic fraction and length cut-offs, alongside a fixed broth-microdilution protocol; sliders in the playground move four properties and recompute a simplified score against the original, with suggestions raised by the same cut-offs

distinctive: the decision threshold is pinned below 0.5 and commented as a deliberate asymmetry, treating a missed positive as costlier than a wasted test
the sequence itself is a view: residues are coloured into charged, hydrophobic and other classes, so the pattern behind the numbers is legible
the radar normalises each property against a stated field-typical range, so the shape reads as in-range or out-of-range rather than as raw units
three models vote, and their disagreement is itself the output — a split vote is reported as borderline rather than averaged away
the slider panel is explicitly a different, simpler scoring function than the main model, labelled as directional intuition only

parts.title: Page navigation and model summary
parts.summary: A dark sidebar that switches between the analysis page and three reference pages, and keeps the model stack, training-set size and headline score in view.

parts.title: Sequence entry and analysis trigger
parts.summary: Lets the person paste a sequence or load a named example, validates its length and alphabet, and runs the prediction and attribution on one button.

parts.title: Prediction and confidence readout
parts.summary: Shows the predicted class, the probability as a large figure with a progress bar, and a confidence band derived from how far the probability sits from the middle.

spans.first: # Scientifically justified for drug discovery context

parts.title: Coloured sequence strip and property chips
parts.summary: Redraws the sequence with each residue coloured by its charge or hydrophobicity class, with a legend and chips carrying the headline physicochemical values.

parts.title: Physicochemical profile radar
parts.summary: Plots five properties of the sequence on one polar axis, each normalised against a field-typical range so the person can see at a glance which sit inside it.

parts.title: Feature contribution breakdown
parts.summary: Ranks the features by how strongly each pushed the prediction, as a diverging bar chart of the top twelve and two signed lists of bars, one per direction.

parts.title: Three-model consensus
parts.summary: Scores the same sequence with all three trained models and resolves their agreement into a vote count, an average probability and a verdict that flags splits as borderline.

parts.title: Full feature table and CSV export
parts.summary: Tables every computed feature with its value and category for the current sequence, and downloads the table as a CSV named after the sequence.

parts.title: Bench guidance keyed to the profile
parts.summary: Turns the computed charge, hydrophobic fraction and length into handling, solubility and stability notes against fixed cut-offs, beside a standard assay protocol card.

parts.title: Property sliders and simplified rescore
parts.summary: Moves four physicochemical properties away from the sequence's own values and recomputes a simplified score, showing it against the original with the change and a reading of the direction.
